title: Booking rack: Total receipt
topics: Greedy choices, dynamic programming and backtracking
summary: Each booking is [start,end] with start < end and occupies [start,end). Sort by end then start ascending; accept a booking if it starts at or after the last accepted end. Produce accepted durations in acceptance order. Negative times are allowed. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
Half-open booking cards compete for a single press whose next job may start exactly when the previous one ends. Ada is closing the print-room account before the afternoon mail. A single total must replace the pile of working slips.

Each booking is [start,end] with start < end and occupies [start,end). Sort by end then start ascending; accept a booking if it starts at or after the last accepted end. Produce accepted durations in acceptance order. Negative times are allowed.

Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement bookingRackTotalReceipt(drawers, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Greedy interval selection. Each booking is [start,end] with start < end and occupies [start,end). Sort by end then start ascending; accept a booking if it starts at or after the last accepted end. Produce accepted durations in acceptance order. Negative times are allowed. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n log n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with greedy interval selection. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

Each booking is [start,end] with start < end and occupies [start,end). Sort by end then start ascending; accept a booking if it starts at or after the last accepted end. Produce accepted durations in acceptance order. Negative times are allowed. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [4,1,1,1,6]. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 13.
The derived sequence is [3,5]. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 8.
The derived sequence is []. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 0.
